Confirmed, and none of the exclusions hold.

Not a GTK limitation. GTK4's own documentation for `gtk_window_is_active` (Gtk-4.0.gir, gtkwindow.c:6009) reads "Returns whether the window is part of the current active toplevel. The active toplevel is the window receiving keystrokes... You might use this function if you wanted to draw a widget differently in an active window from a widget in an inactive window", and the `is-active` property is documented as "Whether the toplevel is the currently active window". It is a per-display singleton and a rendering hint, not an input precondition, so requiring it makes every widget outside the focused toplevel permanently ineligible. Nothing in the userEvent path needs it either: `click` (click.ts `emitGesture`/`emitClickSequence`/`applyClickOutcome`) emits `pressed`/`released` on `Gtk.GestureClick` controllers and calls `widget.activate()`, and `type` (text.ts `focusEditable`/`insertEditableText`) calls `grabFocus` and emits `insert-at-cursor` on the buffer. No GdkEvent is ever pushed through the display, so window activation is irrelevant to whether the emission lands.

Not a machine or MCP artifact. Reproduced by a completely different route than the report: a plain vitest test in a scratch copy of the published-package template (@gtkx/*@1.0.0), with no MCP server, no `gtkx dev`, and no probe client, rendering two sibling `GtkWindow`s and clicking the first window's button after the second opens fails with the identical "did not become actionable within 500ms because its window never became active". A diagnostic run in the same harness printed, stably over 1.3s, `Main active=false visible=true mapped=true focusWidget=true | Extra active=true visible=true mapped=true focusWidget=true`, with the target button `sensitive=true mapped=true canTarget=true`, and `fireEvent(bump, "clicked")` on that same widget incremented the counter. Changing only line 27 of the installed `event-wrapper` (in the scratch copy) to accept the case where some mapped toplevel is active makes the two-window click pass and leaves the single-window template test passing, so the gate is the sole obstacle.

Not a documented misuse. website/guide/modals-and-portals.md:43 documents exactly this shape ("A window element mounts at the top level wherever it sits in the JSX, so opening one is a conditional render"), website/guide/testing.md:55 promises "Queries search every open toplevel", and website/guide/mcp.md says gtkx_click "works on any activatable widget". Neither window is modal or transient-for anything.

Not a missing feature: the check exists and rejects targets that GTK considers perfectly able to receive the emission, and packages/testing/tests/actionability.test.tsx asserts only the insensitive and unmapped branches, so the active branch is an unspecified readiness heuristic rather than intended behavior.

Ledger: this is the same report as U308 (round 3, mcpdrive), which carries no verdict ("Verifier agent died on the session limit; needs re-verification"), so it is the re-verification of U308 rather than a duplicate of a settled finding. F206 concerns a different branch of the same function (a widget with no root treated as actionable) and F207 concerns render resolving before the harness window becomes active; neither covers this.
confirmed.likelyLocation: /home/eugenio/gtkx-bughunt/packages/testing/src/user-event/event-wrapper.ts:27 — the `if (canDisplayDeliverActivation(root) && !root.isActive())` branch of `findWindowActionabilityFailure` (message constant `WINDOW_NOT_ACTIVE` at :10), reached from `waitForActionable` (:56) and `wrapEvent` (:74), which every userEvent helper funnels through (`click` at packages/testing/src/user-event/click.ts:228/243, `type`/`clear` at packages/testing/src/user-event/text.ts:198). The MCP tools reach the same code at packages/cli/src/mcp/handlers.ts:60 and :65.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Fix `findWindowActionabilityFailure` in packages/testing/src/user-event/event-wrapper.ts so the activation clause stops being a per-window requirement and becomes what it was actually meant to be: a barrier that waits until the display has finished handing activation to the process at all. Concretely, keep the sensitive, allocated, and mapped checks unchanged, and replace `!root.isActive()` with a check over `Gtk.Window.listToplevels()` (already the idiomatic enumeration in this package, used by screenshot.ts:330 and matchers.ts:530) that fails only when no mapped toplevel on the display is active, meaning the window is still being presented and the F207-style race is genuinely open; once any toplevel is active, a background window is a background window and its widgets are actionable. The condition the message names must stay one the caller can influence, so rename the constant to say that no window of the application has been activated yet. The one input restriction GTK really imposes belongs there instead of activation: refuse when another visible toplevel holds a modal grab over the target's root (a different visible window with `modal` set that is not the root itself and whose transient-for chain does not lead away from it), with its own message, which also preserves the correct refusal for a modal dialog covering its parent. Add coverage in packages/testing/tests/actionability.test.tsx for both branches: a click and a type into a widget in a second, unfocused toplevel must succeed, and a click into a window blocked by a modal toplevel must fail naming the modal grab.

None of the rule-outs apply, and the defect is GTKX's own naming decision rather than an accommodation it never attempted.

1. GTKX guarantees ESM output through its own transforms, independent of Vite. packages/cli/src/vite-plugins/built-url.ts:16 (`bundleRelativeUrl`) injects `new URL(..., import.meta.url)` and packages/cli/src/vite-plugins/native.ts:48 (`rewriteLoader`) injects `createRequire(import.meta.url)`. Both are unconditional, which is why the emitted artifact's first line begins with an `import.meta.url` reference.

2. Vite already solves the extension question and GTKX overrides it. In the installed vite 8.2.1 (node_modules/vite/dist/node/chunks/node.js:33649) the SSR entry name is `[name].${jsExt}` where `jsExt = resolveOutputJsExtension(format, findNearestPackageData(root)?.data.type)`, and that helper (same file, line 33774) returns `mjs` for the `es` format whenever the nearest package.json type is not "module". `builder.ts` replaces that computed name with the constant "bundle.js", defeating the one mechanism designed to keep an ESM chunk from landing under an extension the package type makes CommonJS. The output-naming logic exists and is wrong, so this is broken behavior, not an unimplemented feature.

3. Nothing in the CLI consults the project's module type. The only read of the project package.json is packages/cli/src/internal/data-dir.ts:46, which looks at `imports` for the `#data` mapping and nothing else. No documentation states the project must be `"type": "module"`: a grep over website/tutorial, website/guide and website/docs turns up no such requirement, and website/tutorial/packaging.md mentions CommonJS only in the opposite direction (the SEA path re-emits the bundle as CJS with esbuild). The reproduction therefore violates no documented constraint.

rejected.why: Ruled out on the duplicate ground. `/home/eugenio/gtkx-bughunt/.bughunt/findings.jsonl` line 55 is F307, whose title is character-for-character this report's title ("A NUL byte in an interpolated style value makes the stylesheet flush throw from a detached microtask, killing the app with an uncatchable error and a message that names no style"), with the same persona (`styling`, round 3), the same surface (`@gtkx/css` — `StyleSheet.scheduleUpdate`, the `queueMicrotask(() => { this.ensureProvider().loadFromString(this.css); })` block), the same severity (`crash`), and the same `likelyLocation` (`/home/eugenio/gtkx-bughunt/packages/css/src/stylesheet.ts:31`, plus `StyleSheet.insert` at :37-40 as the second half). F307 already carries `status: "confirmed"`, and `remediation-3.json` contains only the codegen `resolveStore` hoisting fix, so F307 is still open rather than fixed; this is therefore a re-report of a live ledger entry, not a regression of a repaired one. Confirming it again would double-count the same defect. On the merits the attribution in F307 still holds against the current worktree source, which is unchanged (`packages/css/src/stylesheet.ts` last touched by e679a068 and still shows the unguarded microtask and the append-only `this.css`): GTK4's `gtk_css_provider_load_from_string()` takes a NUL-terminated `const char *`, so a string carrying an interior NUL genuinely cannot be passed and the native string codec is right to reject it; what GTKX owns is (a) raising that rejection from a `queueMicrotask` callback with no user frame beneath it, which Node escalates to an uncaught exception and process exit 1, and (b) leaving the poisoned text in the accumulating `this.css`, so every later `insert` re-throws. Neither of those is GTK behavior being faithfully exposed. None of the other rule-out grounds apply: the repro uses `css` exactly as `website/guide/css.md` teaches, and the failure is in pure JS/FFI marshalling with no dependence on the compositor, system packages, or store freshness. It is still ruled out solely as a duplicate of F307.

rejected.title: npm run flatpak:sources, run in the order the tutorial documents, vendors only the packages npm did not install, so the sandbox build dies on npm ci --offline with ENOTCACHED
rejected.why:
Ruled out on two grounds.

1. Duplicate. /home/eugenio/gtkx-bughunt/.bughunt/findings.jsonl line 66 carries id U309, round 3, persona `deploy`, with a character-for-character identical title, already adjudicated `status: "rejected"`, `isGtkxAtFault: false` (detail: .bughunt/round-3.json rejected[8]).

2. Artifact of a third-party package installed on this machine, re-verified here independently of that record. The vendoring decision is made entirely inside the generator binary, with no GTKX code in the path. /home/eugenio/.local/lib/python3.14/site-packages/flatpak_node_generator/providers/npm.py:111-116, in `NpmLockfileProvider._process_packages_v2`:

    package_json_path = lockfile.parent / install_path / 'package.json'
    if (
        'node_modules' not in package_json_path.parents
        and package_json_path.exists()
    ):
        source = LocalSource(path=install_path)

`Path.parents` yields `PosixPath` objects, so comparing the `str` `'node_modules'` against them never matches. Checked directly: `'node_modules' in PosixPath('/x/node_modules/foo/package.json').parents` is False, so the guard is always true and the condition collapses to `package_json_path.exists()`. Every lockfile entry whose install path is on disk is therefore downgraded from a registry tarball to a LocalSource, which is exactly the 80-of-354 collapse the report measures.

I reproduced the same operation a different way, with zero GTKX code, zero GTKX scripts and no flatpak manifest: a two-dependency project (`ms`, `lodash.merge`, lockfileVersion 3) at /tmp/claude-1001/-home-eugenio-gtkx/e764a39a-058a-4899-a510-52f5d1528812/scratchpad/mini2. The identical `flatpak-node-generator npm package-lock.json -o …` invocation emits 0 of 2 registry tarballs with `node_modules` present, and 2 of 2 with `node_modules` moved aside. Same collapse, no GTKX involvement.

The installed package is a stale unofficial redistribution whose own METADATA reads "this is an unofficial pypi distribution of the flatpak_node_generator script" (`flatpak_node_generator` 0.1.1, the only PyPI release). Upstream has deleted the disk-probing branch: fetching node/flatpak_node_generator/providers/npm.py from flatpak-builder-tools master confirms `_process_packages_v2` makes no `.exists()` call on any filesystem path and decides from the lockfile alone, emitting a LocalSource only for a `file:` resolved URL or for an entry with no `resolved` field.

So examples/tutorial/flatpak/generate-sources.sh:17 issues the invocation the tool's own documentation prescribes, the order in examples/tutorial/flatpak/README.md:22-24 and website/tutorial/flatpak.md is the canonical flow, and `skip: [node_modules]` in com.gtkx.tutorial.yaml:48-49 is standard for a `dir` source. Nothing GTKX ships contradicts its documented contract; the installed generator fails to honor its own.
